[2026-10-21T19:44:16.897Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Chrome for Testing by default\n\nWithout a `channel` or an `executablePath` (`executable_path` in Python and\nRust), every engine starts **Chrome for Testing**: the browser\n`npx playwright install chromium`, `npx puppeteer browsers install chrome`,\n`python -m playwright install chromium` or Selenium Manager downloads. It is\nnever the user's own Google Chrome, so automation does not share an\napplication, a Dock icon or a keychain entry with the browser the person uses\n(issue #179). The installed Google Chrome is started only on request:\n\n| Language   | Chrome for Testing (default)  | The installed Google Chrome                     |\n| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |\n| JavaScript | `launchBrowser({ engine })`   | `launchBrowser({ engine, channel: 'chrome' })`  |\n| Python     | `launch_browser(engine=...)`  | `launch_browser(engine=..., channel=\"chrome\")`  |\n| Rust       | `LaunchOptions::playwright()` | `LaunchOptions::playwright().channel(\"chrome\")` |\n\n## Which download each engine uses\n\n| Engine                        | Chrome for Testing it starts                                                                                                         |\n| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| Playwright, Puppeteer (JS)    | The engine's own `executablePath()`, else the newest build in its download cache.                                                    |\n| Selenium (JS)                 | Playwright's, then Puppeteer's, then the newest cached build, then the one Selenium Manager downloads.                                |\n| Playwright (Python)           | Playwright's `chromium.executable_path`, else the newest build in its download cache.                                                |\n| Selenium (Python)             | Playwright's, then the Playwright, Puppeteer and Selenium Manager caches, then the one Selenium Manager downloads.                    |\n| Rust Playwright, Puppeteer    | The one the Node engine reports, else the newest build in its download cache.                                                        |\n| Rust chromiumoxide            | The newest build in the Playwright, Puppeteer and Selenium Manager caches; chromiumoxide's own detection would find Google Chrome.   |\n| Rust fantoccini (WebDriver)   | The newest cached build whose chromedriver is cached too, else the newest cached build.                                              |\n\nWhen no engine has one, the launch fails with the command that installs it, or\nsays to pass `channel: 'chrome'`; it never falls back to Google Chrome\nsilently. The caches are `ms-playwright` (moved by `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`),\n`~/.cache/puppeteer` (moved by `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR`) and `~/.cache/selenium`\n(moved by `SE_CACHE_PATH`).\n\n## The matching ChromeDriver\n\nSelenium and fantoccini attach through a ChromeDriver, and a ChromeDriver\ndrives only the Chrome major version it was built for. A `chromedriver` on\n`PATH` belongs to the installed Google Chrome, so it is not used for Chrome\nfor Testing; with another release, the session fails with \"This version of\nChromeDriver only supports Chrome version …\".\n\n- **Selenium (JS and Python)** asks Selenium Manager for the driver of the\n  browser that was started (`--browser-path`) and passes\n  `--skip-driver-in-path`, because Selenium Manager would otherwise return the\n  driver on `PATH` whatever its release. Reattaching to a handed-off browser\n  passes its executable again.\n- **Rust fantoccini** uses the chromedriver Selenium Manager or\n  `@puppeteer/browsers` downloaded for the same release, else the newest\n  cached one of the same major version. Playwright downloads no driver: with\n  only Playwright's Chrome for Testing and no cached driver of that major\n  version, the `chromedriver` on `PATH` is used, and must then be of the same\n  major version. `WebDriverOptions::driver_executable` names the driver\n  explicitly.\n\n`cargo run --example engine_chrome_for_testing -- fantoccini` (or\n`chromiumoxide`) starts an engine launch without a channel and prints the\nexecutable, whether it is Chrome for Testing, the default restrictions and the\nuser agent.\n\n## The Linux sandbox on Ubuntu 23.10 and newer\n\nUbuntu 23.10 and newer restrict the unprivileged user namespaces Chromium's\nsandbox needs (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`). Google\nChrome's package installs an AppArmor profile that exempts it; Chrome for\nTesting has none, so it exits with \"No usable sandbox!\" and the launch fails\nwith that line in its stderr. Browser Commander does not add `--no-sandbox` on\nits own, because the command line stays the one a person would type. Fix the\nhost the way\n[Chromium describes](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/security/apparmor-userns-restrictions.md) -\nan AppArmor profile for the Chrome for Testing directory, or\n`sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0` on a disposable\nCI runner - or pass `args: ['--no-sandbox']` (Rust: `.sandbox(false)`) where\nthe sandbox is not wanted.\n\n## Default restrictions: no infobar, no keychain prompt\n\nChrome for Testing shows a \"Chrome for Testing is only for automated testing\"\nbar under the toolbar, and on macOS it asks for the keychain password the first\ntime it encrypts cookies or passwords. A launch of Chrome for Testing therefore\nadds the `chrome-for-testing` preset of\n[launch restrictions](feature-parity.md#launch-command-line-and-opt-in-restrictions):\n\n| Restriction                     | Switch                                                   | Effect                                                                                                                                        |\n| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `no-chrome-for-testing-infobar` | `--test-type=gpu`                                        | Hides the bar. Chromium skips it only for this test type, which also skips the unsupported-flag and other startup infobars, and nothing else. |\n| `mock-keychain`                 | `--use-mock-keychain` (`--password-store=[REDACTED] on Linux) | Encrypts with a fixed key instead of a \"Chromium Safe Storage\" keychain entry, so the OS never prompts.                                        |\n\nAny other browser - Google Chrome, Edge, Brave, Chromium - gets no default\nrestriction. The session reports what was added as `defaultRestrictions`\n(`default_restrictions` in Python and Rust), and `measureParity()` counts these\nswitches as requested. `defaultRestrictions: []` opts out, and any other list\nreplaces the preset.\n\n## Profile migration\n\n`migrateFrom` (`migrate_from`) re-encrypts passwords with the key of the\nbrowser that starts. Chrome for Testing reads \"Chromium Safe Storage\", not\nGoogle Chrome's \"Chrome Safe Storage\", and with the default `mock-keychain`\nrestriction it uses Chromium's fixed mock key (the public `mock_password` on\nmacOS, `peanuts` on Linux) instead, so migrated passwords decrypt in it.\n`targetKeystoreFor(args, platform)` / `target_keystore_for` decide which\nkeystore a command line uses.\n\n## Verifying it\n\n`js/tests/e2e/chrome-for-testing.e2e.test.js` launches each JavaScript engine,\nreads `chrome://version` to check the executable and both switches. The\n`Browser Parity` workflow installs every engine's Chrome for Testing and runs\nit, alongside the Python and Rust default launches.\n"

A launch of Chrome for Testing therefore\nadds the `chrome-for-testing` preset of\n[launch restrictions](feature-parity.md#launch-command-line-and-opt-in-restrictions):\n\n| Restriction                     | Switch                                                   | Effect                                                                                                                                        |\n| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `no-chrome-for-testing-infobar` | `--test-type=gpu`                                        | Hides the bar. Chromium skips it only for this test type, which also skips the unsupported-flag and other startup infobars, and nothing else. |\n| `mock-keychain`                 | `--use-mock-keychain` (`--password-store=[REDACTED] on Linux) | Encrypts with a fixed key instead of a \"Chromium Safe Storage\" keychain entry, so the OS never prompts.                                        |\n\nAny other browser - Google Chrome, Edge, Brave, Chromium - gets no default\nrestriction. The session reports what was added as `defaultRestrictions`\n(`default_restrictions` in Python and Rust), and `measureParity()` counts these\nswitches as requested. `defaultRestrictions: []` opts out, and any other list\nreplaces the preset.\n\n## Profile migration\n\n`migrateFrom` (`migrate_from`) re-encrypts passwords with the key of the\nbrowser that starts. Chrome for Testing reads \"Chromium Safe Storage\", not\nGoogle Chrome's \"Chrome Safe Storage\", and with the default `mock-keychain`\nrestriction it uses Chromium's fixed mock key (the public `mock_password` on\nmacOS, `peanuts` on Linux) instead, so migrated passwords decrypt in it.\n`targetKeystoreFor(args, platform)` / `target_keystore_for` decide which\nkeystore a command line uses.\n\n## Verifying it\n\n`js/tests/e2e/chrome-for-testing.e2e.test.js` launches each JavaScript engine,\nreads `chrome://version` to check the executable and both switches. The\n`Browser Parity` workflow installs every engine's Chrome for Testing and runs\nit, alongside the Python and Rust default launches.\n",

This affected JS real launches and hand-off reattach, Python real launches, and Rust/fantoccini. The driver is now resolved for the browser that was started (Selenium Manager `--browser-path` / `binary_location`). A `chromedriver` on `PATH` is never used for Chrome for Testing.\n- **Linux sandbox.** On Ubuntu 23.10+ (including `ubuntu-24.04` runners), Chrome for Testing has no AppArmor profile and aborts with \"No usable sandbox!\". The library does **not** add `--no-sandbox` by itself, to keep the command line honest. Instead:\n  - [`docs/chrome-for-testing.md`](docs/chrome-for-testing.md) documents the host fixes;\n  - the engine-suites CI job runs `sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`.\n\nDocs: [`docs/chrome-for-testing.md`](docs/chrome-for-testing.md) (new), `docs/feature-parity.md`, `docs/quiet-chrome.md`, and the three READMEs.\n\n## #180: trace and default screenshots are taken without a `clip`\n\n- **Cause.** Trace checkpoint screenshots used the engine's `page.screenshot()`. For the viewport, Playwright sends `Page.captureScreenshot` with a `clip`, and Chrome emulates that size while it captures. A window resized during the capture can stay drawn at the old size.\n- **Fix.** Trace checkpoints, and default captures of a page that has no fixed viewport, now send CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` without a `clip`. This is in `js/src/traces/recorder.js`, `js/src/capture/screenshot.js`, `python/.../capture.py`, `python/.../traces/engine.py`, `rust/src/capture.rs` and `rust/src/traces/page.rs`.\n- **Tests:**\n  - `js/tests/unit/traces/issue-180-screenshots.test.js`, `python/tests/unit/traces/test_issue_180_screenshots.py` and the Rust stub-engine tests assert that no `clip` is sent.\n  - `experiments/issue-180/resize-during-screenshot.mjs` reproduces the resize race against a real browser.\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n- **#179:** on `main`, run `launchBrowser({ engine: 'playwright' })` on a machine with Google Chrome installed. It starts `/Applications/Google Chrome.app` (or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`). Now it starts `chrome-*/chrome` from the Playwright cache, and `chrome://version` shows `--test-type=gpu --use-mock-keychain`. `experiments/issue-179/` holds the probes.\n- **#180:** run `node experiments/issue-180/resize-during-screenshot.mjs`.\n\n## CI fixes needed for this PR (these also fail on `main`)\n\n- **Security:** `chore(deps)` takes the rustls-webpki, launch-editor and markdown-it advisories that were published on 2026-10-20.\n- **CI Workflow Policy:** zizmor's `ref-version-mismatch` fired at `safari.yml:79` because upstream moved `v2` of `Swatinem/rust-cache`. The comment now names the exact version the SHA points to, `v2.9.2`.\n- **Broken Link Checker:** `chromium.googlesource.com` answered 503 and then let the re-check time out. A 5xx followed by a timeout is now reported as transient, not gone. Test: \"does not fail for a host that answered 5xx and then timed out\".\n\n## CodeQL notes\n\nCodeQL flags `rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value` at `rust/src/browser/migration/os_crypt_keys.rs:173,175` and in its tests. The flagged strings are `mock_password` and `peanuts`. These are Chromium's public, fixed passwords for the mock keychain and the Linux basic store, not secrets. `main` uses the same constants in `browser_cookies.rs` and `os_crypt_keys.rs`, and the alerts on those lines (for example #35, #67 and #68) are dismissed as false positives. These new alerts should be dismissed the same way.\n\n## Local checks\n\n- **JS:** `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication`, and the changeset validation.\n- [2026-10-21T20:04:35.541Z] [INFO]           "content": "## Summary\n\n#185 asks for one pull request that addresses #179, #180, #181 and #183. **All four were already resolved by #184**, which merged into `main` on 2026-10-21 and closed them. This PR therefore keeps `main`'s implementation (`main` is merged in) and adds only the #179 gaps that `main` still had. Each gap was confirmed against `main` and gets a test that fails without its fix. The closing references stay, so merging also closes #185:\n\nFixes #185\nFixes #179\nFixes #180\nFixes #181\nFixes #183\n\n| Issue | Status |\n| --- | --- |\n| #179 Chrome for Testing by default, no infobar, no keychain prompt | Resolved by #184. This PR fixes the ChromeDriver mismatch, the password-migration key, the Rust chromiumoxide engine and the Python parity count, as described below. |\n| #180 Trace screenshots without a `clip` | Resolved by #184; no further changes. |\n| #181, #183 \"Address all open issues\" | Tracking issues whose sub-issues (#179, #180, #181) are resolved by #184. |\n\n## What `main` still got wrong, and the fixes\n\n### 1. Selenium / fantoccini used the wrong ChromeDriver for Chrome for Testing\n\nChromeDriver drives only its own Chrome major version. A `chromedriver` on `PATH` belongs to the installed Google Chrome, and Selenium Manager returns that one too unless it is given `--skip-driver-in-path`. So on a machine with Chrome 155 and ChromeDriver on `PATH`, Chrome for Testing 156 failed with `session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 155`.\n\n- **JS** (`webdriver.js`, `real-browser.js`, `browser-handoff.js`): the driver is resolved for the browser that was started. A `PATH` driver is skipped for Chrome for Testing, and Selenium Manager gets `--browser-path` and `--skip-driver-in-path`. A real-browser Selenium attach and the hand-off reattach also pass the executable. `defaultRestrictionsFor` is exported.\n- **Python** (`launch_executable.chrome_for_testing_driver`, `connector.py`, `real_browser.py`, `launcher.py`): same behaviour, through `binary_location` and Selenium Manager.\n- **Rust fantoccini** (`chrome_for_testing.rs`, `webdriver/mod.rs`, `engine_launch.rs`): without a `driver_executable`, it uses the chromedriver that Selenium Manager or `@puppeteer/browsers` downloaded for the same release, else the newest cached one of the same major version. An engine launch prefers a Chrome for Testing download whose driver is cached.\n- **Tests:**\n  - JS: `webdriver.test.js`, `real-browser.test.js`, `browser-handoff.test.js`\n  - Python: `test_issue_179_chromedriver.py`\n  - Rust: `chrome_for_testing_tests.rs`, `webdriver::driver_tests`, `engine_launch_tests.rs`\n\n### 2. Rust chromiumoxide engine launches started the installed Google Chrome\n\n`LaunchOptions::chromiumoxide()` without a channel left browser discovery to chromiumoxide, which finds Google Chrome, with no default restrictions. It now starts the newest cached Chrome for Testing with the `chrome-for-testing` preset, and fails with the install hint when there is none (`engine_launch_tests.rs`).\n\nReal run with ChromeDriver 153 on `PATH`, Google Chrome 155 installed and Playwright's Chrome for Testing 156 cached (`cargo run --example engine_chrome_for_testing -- <engine>`):\n\n- **`main`** ([`experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt`](experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt)):\n  - fantoccini: `session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 153`\n  - chromiumoxide: `chrome for testing: false`, `default restrictions: []`, `HeadlessChrome/155`\n- **This branch** ([`experiments/rust-engine-after-branch.txt`](experiments/rust-engine-after-branch.txt)): both engines report `.../ms-playwright/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome`, `chrome for testing: true`, `[\"no-chrome-for-testing-infobar\", \"mock-keychain\"]` and `HeadlessChrome/156`.\n\n### 3. Profile migration encrypted passwords with Google Chrome's key\n\n`migrateFrom` re-encrypted passwords with the key of the requested channel. Chrome for Testing reads \"Chromium Safe Storage\", and with its default `--use-mock-keychain` it reads Chromium's fixed mock key, so migrated passwords did not decrypt. The target key now follows the browser that actually starts:\n\n- `chromium` for Chrome for Testing.\n- The mock key (`mock_password` on macOS, `peanuts` on Linux, prefix `v10`) when the command line has `--use-mock-keychain` (macOS) or `--password-store=[REDACTED] (Linux).\n- macOS logins use the `v10` prefix Chromium writes there.\n\nThis applies in all three languages: `targetKeystoreFor` / `target_keystore_for` / `TargetKeystore`.\n\n- **Tests:**\n  - `os-crypt-keys.test.js`, `real-browser.test.js`, `safari-data.test.js`\n  - `test_os_crypt_keys.py`, `test_issue_179_chromedriver.py`\n  - `migration/tests/os_crypt_keys.rs`, `real_browser_tests::migrates_passwords_with_the_key_of_the_browser_that_starts`\n\n### 4. Python `measure_parity` treated Chrome for Testing's default switches as unrequested\n\n`_requested_args_for` counted the restriction switches only when the caller passed `restrictions`. Test: `test_parity_counts_the_default_restrictions_as_requested`.\n\n### Docs and CI\n\n- New [`docs/chrome-for-testing.md`](docs/chrome-for-testing.md), linked from the four READMEs. It covers which download each engine starts, the matching ChromeDriver, the Ubuntu 23.10+ AppArmor sandbox (the library does not add `--no-sandbox` on its own) and the migration key.\n- `js/tests/e2e/chrome-for-testing.e2e.test.js` checks `chrome://version` for each JS engine. The `Browser Parity` workflow installs each engine's Chrome for Testing, lifts the AppArmor userns restriction on its runner, and runs the suite.\n- Broken Link Checker:\n  - `chromium.googlesource.com` answered 503 and then timed out; a 5xx followed by a timeout now counts as transient.\n  - Links to files this branch adds are accepted.\n  - The `rust-cache` pin comment names its exact version.\n\n## How to reproduce on `main`\n\n1. Install Google Chrome with its `chromedriver` on `PATH`, and run `npx playwright install chromium`.\n2. Run `launchBrowser({ engine: 'selenium' })` in JS, or `launch_real_browser(RealBrowserOptions(engine=\"selenium\"))` in Python. The ChromeDriver version error appears.\n3. Run `cargo run --example engine_chrome_for_testing -- chromiumoxide` (in Rust). It reports Google Chrome.\n4. Run `launchRealBrowser({ migrateFrom: { browser: 'chrome' } })` on macOS. Passwords show as undecryptable in Chrome for Testing.\n\n## Notes\n\n- **CodeQL** flags `rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value` on `mock_password` and `peanuts`. These are Chromium's public, fixed mock-keychain and basic-store passwords, not secrets. `main` already uses them in `browser_cookies.rs`, where the same alerts were dismissed as false positives.\n- **Safari (python)** on bf0b147 was cancelled before any step ran: no macOS runner was assigned (`runner_name` empty, 0 steps), which is runner allocation on GitHub's side. Later pushes rerun it.\n\n## Local checks\n\n- **JS:** `npm test` (1948 pass), `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication`, and `validate-changeset.mjs`.\n- **Python:** `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src`, and `pytest tests/unit` (1346 passed).\n- **Rust:**\n  - `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -Dwarnings` pass.\n  - `cargo test --all-features`: 716 lib tests and every integration suite passed. The local run reached its time limit during the doctests, which CI runs.\n  - `check-file-size.mjs` passes.\n- **Repo:** `check-file-line-limits.sh`, `generate-feature-parity.mjs --check`, and ESLint over `scripts`, `experiments` and `rust/scripts`.\n\nRelease notes:\n\n- `js/.changeset/chrome-for-testing-chromedriver.md` (patch)\n- `python/changelog.d/179-{chromedriver,migration,parity}.fixed.md`\n- `rust/changelog.d/20261021_200000_engine_chrome_for_testing.md` and `20261021_201000_chrome_for_testing_migration_key.md` (patch)\n"

This PR therefore keeps `main`'s implementation (`main` is merged in) and adds only the #179 gaps that `main` still had. Each gap was confirmed against `main` and gets a test that fails without its fix. The closing references stay, so merging also closes #185:\n\nFixes #185\nFixes #179\nFixes #180\nFixes #181\nFixes #183\n\n| Issue | Status |\n| --- | --- |\n| #179 Chrome for Testing by default, no infobar, no keychain prompt | Resolved by #184. This PR fixes the ChromeDriver mismatch, the password-migration key, the Rust chromiumoxide engine and the Python parity count, as described below. |\n| #180 Trace screenshots without a `clip` | Resolved by #184; no further changes. |\n| #181, #183 \"Address all open issues\" | Tracking issues whose sub-issues (#179, #180, #181) are resolved by #184. |\n\n## What `main` still got wrong, and the fixes\n\n### 1. Selenium / fantoccini used the wrong ChromeDriver for Chrome for Testing\n\nChromeDriver drives only its own Chrome major version. A `chromedriver` on `PATH` belongs to the installed Google Chrome, and Selenium Manager returns that one too unless it is given `--skip-driver-in-path`. So on a machine with Chrome 155 and ChromeDriver on `PATH`, Chrome for Testing 156 failed with `session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 155`.\n\n- **JS** (`webdriver.js`, `real-browser.js`, `browser-handoff.js`): the driver is resolved for the browser that was started. A `PATH` driver is skipped for Chrome for Testing, and Selenium Manager gets `--browser-path` and `--skip-driver-in-path`. A real-browser Selenium attach and the hand-off reattach also pass the executable. `defaultRestrictionsFor` is exported.\n- **Python** (`launch_executable.chrome_for_testing_driver`, `connector.py`, `real_browser.py`, `launcher.py`): same behaviour, through `binary_location` and Selenium Manager.\n- **Rust fantoccini** (`chrome_for_testing.rs`, `webdriver/mod.rs`, `engine_launch.rs`): without a `driver_executable`, it uses the chromedriver that Selenium Manager or `@puppeteer/browsers` downloaded for the same release, else the newest cached one of the same major version. An engine launch prefers a Chrome for Testing download whose driver is cached.\n- **Tests:**\n  - JS: `webdriver.test.js`, `real-browser.test.js`, `browser-handoff.test.js`\n  - Python: `test_issue_179_chromedriver.py`\n  - Rust: `chrome_for_testing_tests.rs`, `webdriver::driver_tests`, `engine_launch_tests.rs`\n\n### 2. Rust chromiumoxide engine launches started the installed Google Chrome\n\n`LaunchOptions::chromiumoxide()` without a channel left browser discovery to chromiumoxide, which finds Google Chrome, with no default restrictions. It now starts the newest cached Chrome for Testing with the `chrome-for-testing` preset, and fails with the install hint when there is none (`engine_launch_tests.rs`).\n\nReal run with ChromeDriver 153 on `PATH`, Google Chrome 155 installed and Playwright's Chrome for Testing 156 cached (`cargo run --example engine_chrome_for_testing -- <engine>`):\n\n- **`main`** ([`experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt`](experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt)):\n  - fantoccini: `session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 153`\n  - chromiumoxide: `chrome for testing: false`, `default restrictions: []`, `HeadlessChrome/155`\n- **This branch** ([`experiments/rust-engine-after-branch.txt`](experiments/rust-engine-after-branch.txt)): both engines report `.../ms-playwright/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome`, `chrome for testing: true`, `[\"no-chrome-for-testing-infobar\", \"mock-keychain\"]` and `HeadlessChrome/156`.\n\n### 3. Profile migration encrypted passwords with Google Chrome's key\n\n`migrateFrom` re-encrypted passwords with the key of the requested channel. Chrome for Testing reads \"Chromium Safe Storage\", and with its default `--use-mock-keychain` it reads Chromium's fixed mock key, so migrated passwords did not decrypt. The target key now follows the browser that actually starts:\n\n- `chromium` for Chrome for Testing.\n- The mock key (`mock_password` on macOS, `peanuts` on Linux, prefix `v10`) when the command line has `--use-mock-keychain` (macOS) or `--password-store=[REDACTED] (Linux).\n- macOS logins use the `v10` prefix Chromium writes there.\n\nThis applies in all three languages: `targetKeystoreFor` / `target_keystore_for` / `TargetKeystore`.\n\n- **Tests:**\n  - `os-crypt-keys.test.js`, `real-browser.test.js`, `safari-data.test.js`\n  - `test_os_crypt_keys.py`, `test_issue_179_chromedriver.py`\n  - `migration/tests/os_crypt_keys.rs`, `real_browser_tests::migrates_passwords_with_the_key_of_the_browser_that_starts`\n\n### 4. Python `measure_parity` treated Chrome for Testing's default switches as unrequested\n\n`_requested_args_for` counted the restriction switches only when the caller passed `restrictions`. Test: `test_parity_counts_the_default_restrictions_as_requested`.\n\n### Docs and CI\n\n- New [`docs/chrome-for-testing.md`](docs/chrome-for-testing.md), linked from the four READMEs. It covers which download each engine starts, the matching ChromeDriver, the Ubuntu 23.10+ AppArmor sandbox (the library does not add `--no-sandbox` on its own) and the migration key.\n- `js/tests/e2e/chrome-for-testing.e2e.test.js` checks `chrome://version` for each JS engine. The `Browser Parity` workflow installs each engine's Chrome for Testing, lifts the AppArmor userns restriction on its runner, and runs the suite.\n- Broken Link Checker:\n  - `chromium.googlesource.com` answered 503 and then timed out; a 5xx followed by a timeout now counts as transient.\n  - Links to files this branch adds are accepted.\n  - The `rust-cache` pin comment names its exact version.\n\n## How to reproduce on `main`\n\n1. Install Google Chrome with its `chromedriver` on `PATH`, and run `npx playwright install chromium`.\n2. Run `launchBrowser({ engine: 'selenium' })` in JS, or `launch_real_browser(RealBrowserOptions(engine=\"selenium\"))` in Python. The ChromeDriver version error appears.\n3. Run `cargo run --example engine_chrome_for_testing -- chromiumoxide` (in Rust). It reports Google Chrome.\n4. Run `launchRealBrowser({ migrateFrom: { browser: 'chrome' } })` on macOS. Passwords show as undecryptable in Chrome for Testing.\n\n## Notes\n\n- **CodeQL** flags `rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value` on `mock_password` and `peanuts`. Each fix is made in JavaScript, Python and Rust, and the shared parity catalogue and docs are updated with it.\n\nFixes #185\nFixes #179\nFixes #180\nFixes #181\nFixes #183\n\n#181 and #183 are tracking issues. Their only requirement is to resolve #179 and #180 (and, for #183, #181) in one pull request, and this PR does that.\n\n## #179: Chrome for Testing by default, with no infobar and no keychain prompts\n\n| Requested in #179 | Implementation | Tests |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `resolveLaunchExecutable()` starts Chrome for Testing by default, not the user's Google Chrome | **JS:** `js/src/browser/launch-executable.js` uses Playwright's or Puppeteer's download. Selenium uses one of those, and otherwise asks Selenium Manager for `--force-browser-download`. **Python:** `browser/launch_executable.py` uses Playwright's download, otherwise Selenium Manager's. **Rust:** `launch_executable.rs` takes the path Playwright or Puppeteer reports through Node, otherwise the newest download in the caches. In every language, Google Chrome starts only for `channel: 'chrome'` or an `executablePath`. With no Chrome for Testing installed, the launch fails and the error gives the install command; it never falls back to Google Chrome. | `launch-executable.test.js`, `launcher.test.js`, `webdriver.test.js`, `test_issue_179_chrome_for_testing.py`, `test_launch_browser.py`, `launch_executable_tests.rs`, `engine_launch_tests.rs` |\n| Default restriction `no-chrome-for-testing-infobar` (`--test-type=gpu`) for Chrome for Testing | New restriction and a new `chrome-for-testing` preset in the shared `launch-restrictions.json`. `defaultRestrictionsFor(path, requested)` / `default_restrictions_for` applies the preset only when `isChromeForTesting(path)` matches. Any other browser keeps the command line a person would type. `defaultRestrictions: []` turns the preset off. The session reports what was added as `defaultRestrictions`, and `measureParity()` counts those switches as requested. | Same unit suites, plus `parity.test.js`, `real-browser.test.js` and `real_browser_tests.rs` |\n| `--use-mock-keychain` by default for Chrome for Testing | Part of the same preset. Profile migration (`migrateFrom`) now encrypts with the key of the browser that actually starts: Chromium's fixed mock key, or Chrome for Testing's own \"Chromium Safe Storage\" entry. Before, it used Google Chrome's key, so migrated passwords and cookies did not decrypt. | `os-crypt-keys.test.js`, `test_os_crypt_keys.py`, `rust/src/browser/migration/tests/os_crypt_keys.rs` |\n| Tests for each | `js/tests/e2e/chrome-for-testing.e2e.test.js` starts each JS engine headfully. It reads `chrome://version` to check the executable and both switches. It also measures that the window launched with `defaultRestrictions: []` is taller by the infobar's height. The `Browser Parity` workflow now installs each engine's Chrome for Testing and runs this suite. | CI `Engine lifecycle suites (real Chrome)` |\n\nProblems found and fixed along the way:\n\n- **ChromeDriver version.** Selenium resolved ChromeDriver for the installed Google Chrome, and that driver refuses Chrome for Testing. This affected JS real launches and hand-off reattach, Python real launches, and Rust/fantoccini. The driver is now resolved for the browser that was started (Selenium Manager `--browser-path` / `binary_location`). A `chromedriver` on `PATH` is never used for Chrome for Testing.\n- **Linux sandbox.** On Ubuntu 23.10+ (including `ubuntu-24.04` runners), Chrome for Testing has no AppArmor profile and aborts with \"No usable sandbox!\". The library does **not** add `--no-sandbox` by itself, to keep the command line honest. Instead:\n  - [`docs/chrome-for-testing.md`](docs/chrome-for-testing.md) documents the host fixes;\n  - the engine-suites CI job runs `sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`.\n\nDocs: [`docs/chrome-for-testing.md`](docs/chrome-for-testing.md) (new), `docs/feature-parity.md`, `docs/quiet-chrome.md`, and the three READMEs.\n\n## #180: trace and default screenshots are taken without a `clip`\n\n- **Cause.** Trace checkpoint screenshots used the engine's `page.screenshot()`. For the viewport, Playwright sends `Page.captureScreenshot` with a `clip`, and Chrome emulates that size while it captures. A window resized during the capture can stay drawn at the old size.\n- **Fix.** Trace checkpoints, and default captures of a page that has no fixed viewport, now send CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` without a `clip`. This is in `js/src/traces/recorder.js`, `js/src/capture/screenshot.js`, `python/.../capture.py`, `python/.../traces/engine.py`, `rust/src/capture.rs` and `rust/src/traces/page.rs`.\n- **Tests:**\n  - `js/tests/unit/traces/issue-180-screenshots.test.js`, `python/tests/unit/traces/test_issue_180_screenshots.py` and the Rust stub-engine tests assert that no `clip` is sent.\n  - `experiments/issue-180/resize-during-screenshot.mjs` reproduces the resize race against a real browser.\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n- **#179:** on `main`, run `launchBrowser({ engine: 'playwright' })` on a machine with Google Chrome installed. It starts `/Applications/Google Chrome.app` (or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`). Now it starts `chrome-*/chrome` from the Playwright cache, and `chrome://version` shows `--test-type=gpu --use-mock-keychain`. `experiments/issue-179/` holds the probes.\n- **#180:** run `node experiments/issue-180/resize-during-screenshot.mjs`.\n\n## CI fixes needed for this PR (these also fail on `main`)\n\n- **Security:** `chore(deps)` takes the rustls-webpki, launch-editor and markdown-it advisories that were published on 2026-10-20.\n- **CI Workflow Policy:** zizmor's `ref-version-mismatch` fired at `safari.yml:79` because upstream moved `v2` of `Swatinem/rust-cache`. The comment now names the exact version the SHA points to, `v2.9.2`.\n- **Broken Link Checker:** `chromium.googlesource.com` answered 503 and then let the re-check time out. A 5xx followed by a timeout is now reported as transient, not gone. Test: \"does not fail for a host that answered 5xx and then timed out\".\n\n## CodeQL notes\n\nCodeQL flags `rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value` at `rust/src/browser/migration/os_crypt_keys.rs:173,175` and in its tests. The flagged strings are `mock_password` and `peanuts`. These are Chromium's public, fixed passwords for the mock keychain and the Linux basic store, not secrets. `main` uses the same constants in `browser_cookies.rs` and `os_crypt_keys.rs`, and the alerts on those lines (for example #35, #67 and #68) are dismissed as false positives. They now use the driver for the browser that actually starts.\n2. **The Rust chromiumoxide engine started the installed Google Chrome.** It now starts the newest downloaded Chrome for Testing, with its default settings that hide the testing bar and avoid the macOS keychain prompt. If none is downloaded, it fails with the install command. I checked this with real runs before and after; the logs are in `experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt` and `experiments/rust-engine-after-branch.txt`.\n3. **Migrated passwords didn't decrypt.** Migration encrypted them with Google Chrome's key, but Chrome for Testing reads Chromium's. They are now encrypted with the key of the browser that starts, in JS, Python and Rust.\n4. **Python's `measure_parity` miscounted.** It treated Chrome for Testing's default switches as switches nobody asked for.\n\nI also added `docs/chrome-for-testing.md`, linked from the four READMEs, plus release notes for each language.\n\nThe PR description has `Fixes` lines for #185, #179, #180, #181 and #183, so merging closes #185 as well. #185 has stayed open only because its description has unchecked task items.\n\nThings to know before merging:\n- **CodeQL alerts:** CodeQL left 7 review comments flagging `mock_password` and `peanuts` as hard-coded passwords. These are Chromium's publicly known fixed keys, not secrets. `main` already uses them in `browser_cookies.rs`, where the same alerts were dismissed as false positives, so I expect these need dismissing the same way.\n- **Safari (python) check:** on an earlier commit it was cancelled because GitHub never assigned a macOS runner. It passed on the latest commit.\n- **Rust tests locally:** the local `cargo test` run hit its time limit during the doctests, after every other test had passed. CI ran the full suite, doctests included, on Linux, macOS and Windows.\n\nThere are no other comments on the PR or the issue.",

Problem\n\nA browser started for automation must not take over the user's own browser or obstruct the view. In browser-commander 0.28.0, three things go wrong by default on macOS:\n\n1. **Chrome for Testing shows a bar over every page:** «Chrome for Testing v156.0.8078.4 is only for automated testing. For regular browsing, use a standard version of Chrome. [Download Chrome]». It takes vertical space in every window. `--disable-infobars` (the `no-infobars` restriction) does not remove it.\n2. **The user's Google Chrome is taken over:** `resolveLaunchExecutable()` prefers the installed Google Chrome (`channel: 'chrome'`). Started with another `--user-data-dir`, it is still the same app (`com.google.Chrome`) to macOS. When the user's own Chrome is not running, a click on Chrome in the Dock, ⌘T, or a link opened from another app goes to the automation window. An automation that keeps one tab then closes the user's tab.\n3. **The keychain is asked again and again:** Chrome for Testing started without `--use-mock-keychain` asks «Google Chrome for Testing wants to access key \"Chromium Safe Storage\" in your keychain» at each start.\n\n## Root cause and fix\n\n1. Chromium shows the Chrome for Testing bar unless `--test-type=gpu` is given. This is the only command-line value that skips it, from `chrome/browser/ui/startup/infobar_utils.cc`:\n   ```cpp\n   #if BUILDFLAG(CHROME_FOR_TESTING)\n   bool IsGpuTest() {\n     return base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()->GetSwitchValueASCII(switches::kTestType) == \"gpu\";\n   }\n   #endif\n   ...\n   if (show_bad_flags_security_warnings) {\n   #if BUILDFLAG(CHROME_FOR_TESTING)\n     if (!IsGpuTest()) { ... ChromeForTestingInfoBarDelegate::Create(); }\n   #endif\n   ```\n   The only other way is the `CommandLineFlagSecurityWarningsEnabled` policy. `--test-type` also skips the later infobars (session crashed, default browser, …) and does not turn `navigator.webdriver` on.\n2. Launch Chrome for Testing (Playwright's or Puppeteer's), which is an app of its own (`com.google.chrome.for.testing`), and never the user's Google Chrome. The installed Google Chrome should be used only on request.\n3. Pass `--use-mock-keychain` to Chrome for Testing, so the keychain is never asked. Logins moved from a Google Chrome profile can be read by Google Chrome headless, which already has access to its own keychain entry, and then set with `Storage.setCookies`.\n\n## Requested\n\n- A default launch restriction `no-chrome-for-testing-infobar` (`--test-type=gpu`) whenever the executable is Chrome for Testing.\n- `resolveLaunchExecutable()` defaults to Chrome for Testing for automation, not to the user's Google Chrome.\n- `--use-mock-keychain` by default for Chrome for Testing.\n- Tests for each of these.\n\nThe hh-job-application-automation app works around this in `src/browser-session.mjs` (commit a868526 in Problem\n\nA headful page that is being traced (`startTrace`, default `screenshots: 'checkpoints'`) can stop following its window size. After the user resizes the window, the page is still drawn at the old size in the top-left corner and the rest of the window stays blank. It stays that way until the page is reloaded.\n\nBy default, the browser must look and behave exactly like a real browser.\n\n## Cause\n\nThe trace recorder takes checkpoint screenshots with the engine's `page.screenshot({ type: 'png' })` (`src/traces/recorder.js`, `screenshot()`). For a viewport screenshot, Playwright 1.64 sends `Page.captureScreenshot` with a `clip` set to the current viewport. Chrome emulates the clip's size while it captures. If the window is resized during the capture, the emulated size can stay in place after the capture ends.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nMeasured with Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4 on macOS, Playwright 1.64, browser-commander 0.28 (0.32.1 has the same code):\n\n1. Start a headful Chrome and attach with `connectBrowser({ engine: 'playwright', cdpEndpoint })`.\n2. Keep taking screenshots in a loop while the window is resized in about 20 steps with `Browser.setWindowBounds`.\n3. Compare `innerWidth` with `outerWidth`.\n\n| Screenshot method | Drags where the page got stuck |\n|---|---|\n| `page.screenshot({ type: 'png' })` (Playwright) | 2 of 8 |\n| CDP `Page.captureScreenshot { format: 'png' }` (no clip) | 0 of 8 |\n| CDP `Page.captureScreenshot { fromSurface: false, captureBeyondViewport: false }` | 0 of 8 |\n| Trace checkpoints with the no-clip capture | 0 of 12 |\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nFor trace checkpoint screenshots, and any default capture of a page with no fixed viewport, use CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` without a `clip`. `captureStableViewport` already does this when `viewportSize()` is null.\n\nWorkaround in hh-job-application-automation: pass `startTrace` a `page` whose `screenshot` is the CDP capture without a clip.\n","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/180/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/180/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":"completed","pinned_comment":null},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/181","repository_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/browser-commander","labels_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/181/labels{/name}","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/181/comments","events_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/181/events","html_url":"https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/181","id":5963138805,"node_id":"I_kwDOQYTTi88AAAABY25G9Q","number":181,"title":"Address Started with another `--user-data-dir`, it is still the same app (`com.google.Chrome`) to macOS. When the user's own Chrome is not running, a click on Chrome in the Dock, ⌘T, or a link opened from another app goes to the automation window. An automation that keeps one tab then closes the user's tab.\n3. **The keychain is asked again and again:** Chrome for Testing started without `--use-mock-keychain` asks «Google Chrome for Testing wants to access key \"Chromium Safe Storage\" in your keychain» at each start.\n\n## Root cause and fix\n\n1. Chromium shows the Chrome for Testing bar unless `--test-type=gpu` is given. This is the only command-line value that skips it, from `chrome/browser/ui/startup/infobar_utils.cc`:\n   ```cpp\n   #if BUILDFLAG(CHROME_FOR_TESTING)\n   bool IsGpuTest() {\n     return base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()->GetSwitchValueASCII(switches::kTestType) == \"gpu\";\n   }\n   #endif\n   ...\n   if (show_bad_flags_security_warnings) {\n   #if BUILDFLAG(CHROME_FOR_TESTING)\n     if (!IsGpuTest()) { ... ChromeForTestingInfoBarDelegate::Create(); }\n   #endif\n   ```\n   The only other way is the `CommandLineFlagSecurityWarningsEnabled` policy. `--test-type` also skips the later infobars (session crashed, default browser, …) and does not turn `navigator.webdriver` on.\n2. Launch Chrome for Testing (Playwright's or Puppeteer's), which is an app of its own (`com.google.chrome.for.testing`), and never the user's Google Chrome. The installed Google Chrome should be used only on request.\n3. Pass `--use-mock-keychain` to Chrome for Testing, so the keychain is never asked. Logins moved from a Google Chrome profile can be read by Google Chrome headless, which already has access to its own keychain entry, and then set with `Storage.setCookies`.\n\n## Requested\n\n- A default launch restriction `no-chrome-for-testing-infobar` (`--test-type=gpu`) whenever the executable is Chrome for Testing.\n- `resolveLaunchExecutable()` defaults to Chrome for Testing for automation, not to the user's Google Chrome.\n- `--use-mock-keychain` by default for Chrome for Testing.\n- Tests for each of these.\n\nThe hh-job-application-automation app works around this in `src/browser-session.mjs` (commit a868526 in Problem\n\nA headful page that is being traced (`startTrace`, default `screenshots: 'checkpoints'`) can stop following its window size. After the user resizes the window, the page is still drawn at the old size in the top-left corner and the rest of the window stays blank. It stays that way until the page is reloaded.\n\nBy default, the browser must look and behave exactly like a real browser.\n\n## Cause\n\nThe trace recorder takes checkpoint screenshots with the engine's `page.screenshot({ type: 'png' })` (`src/traces/recorder.js`, `screenshot()`). For a viewport screenshot, Playwright 1.64 sends `Page.captureScreenshot` with a `clip` set to the current viewport. Chrome emulates the clip's size while it captures. If the window is resized during the capture, the emulated size can stay in place after the capture ends.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nMeasured with Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4 on macOS, Playwright 1.64, browser-commander 0.28 (0.32.1 has the same code):\n\n1. Start a headful Chrome and attach with `connectBrowser({ engine: 'playwright', cdpEndpoint })`.\n2. Keep taking screenshots in a loop while the window is resized in about 20 steps with `Browser.setWindowBounds`.\n3. Compare `innerWidth` with `outerWidth`.\n\n| Screenshot method | Drags where the page got stuck |\n|---|---|\n| `page.screenshot({ type: 'png' })` (Playwright) | 2 of 8 |\n| CDP `Page.captureScreenshot { format: 'png' }` (no clip) | 0 of 8 |\n| CDP `Page.captureScreenshot { fromSurface: false, captureBeyondViewport: false }` | 0 of 8 |\n| Trace checkpoints with the no-clip Selenium / fantoccini used the wrong ChromeDriver for Chrome for Testing\n\nChromeDriver drives only its own Chrome major version. A `chromedriver` on `PATH` belongs to the installed Google Chrome, and Selenium Manager returns that one too unless it is given `--skip-driver-in-path`. So on a machine with Chrome 155 and ChromeDriver on `PATH`, Chrome for Testing 156 failed with `session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 155`.\n\n- **JS** (`webdriver.js`, `real-browser.js`, `browser-handoff.js`): the driver is resolved for the browser that was started. A `PATH` driver is skipped for Chrome for Testing, and Selenium Manager gets `--browser-path` and `--skip-driver-in-path`. A real-browser Selenium attach and the hand-off reattach also pass the executable. `defaultRestrictionsFor` is exported.\n- **Python** (`launch_executable.chrome_for_testing_driver`, `connector.py`, `real_browser.py`, `launcher.py`): same behaviour, through `binary_location` and Selenium Manager.\n- **Rust fantoccini** (`chrome_for_testing.rs`, `webdriver/mod.rs`, `engine_launch.rs`): without a `driver_executable`, it uses the chromedriver that Selenium Manager or `@puppeteer/browsers` downloaded for the same release, else the newest cached one of the same major version. An engine launch prefers a Chrome for Testing download whose driver is cached.\n- **Tests:**\n  - JS: `webdriver.test.js`, `real-browser.test.js`, `browser-handoff.test.js`\n  - Python: `test_issue_179_chromedriver.py`\n  - Rust: `chrome_for_testing_tests.rs`, `webdriver::driver_tests`, `engine_launch_tests.rs`\n\n### 2. Rust chromiumoxide engine launches started the installed Google Chrome\n\n`LaunchOptions::chromiumoxide()` without a channel left browser discovery to chromiumoxide, which finds Google Chrome, with no default restrictions. It now starts the newest cached Chrome for Testing with the `chrome-for-testing` preset, and fails with the install hint when there is none (`engine_launch_tests.rs`).\n\nReal run with ChromeDriver 153 on `PATH`, Google Chrome 155 installed and Playwright's Chrome for Testing 156 cached (`cargo run --example engine_chrome_for_testing -- <engine>`):\n\n- **`main`** ([`experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt`](experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt)):\n  - fantoccini: `session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 153`\n  - chromiumoxide: `chrome for testing: false`, `default restrictions: []`, `HeadlessChrome/155`\n- **This branch** ([`experiments/rust-engine-after-branch.txt`](experiments/rust-engine-after-branch.txt)): both engines report `.../ms-playwright/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome`, `chrome for testing: true`, `[\"no-chrome-for-testing-infobar\", \"mock-keychain\"]` and `HeadlessChrome/156`.\n\n### 3. Profile migration encrypted passwords with Google Chrome's key\n\n`migrateFrom` re-encrypted passwords with the key of the requested channel. Chrome for Testing reads \"Chromium Safe Storage\", and with its default `--use-mock-keychain` it reads Chromium's fixed mock key, so migrated passwords did not decrypt. The target key now follows the browser that actually starts:\n\n- `chromium` for Chrome for Testing.\n- The mock key (`mock_password` on macOS, `peanuts` on Linux, prefix `v10`) when the command line has `--use-mock-keychain` (macOS) or `--password-store=[REDACTED] (Linux).\n- macOS logins use the `v10` prefix Chromium writes there.\n\nThis applies in all three languages: `targetKeystoreFor` / `target_keystore_for` / `TargetKeystore`.\n\n- **Tests:**\n  - `os-crypt-keys.test.js`, `real-browser.test.js`, `safari-data.test.js`\n  - `test_os_crypt_keys.py`, `test_issue_179_chromedriver.py`\n  - `migration/tests/os_crypt_keys.rs`, `real_browser_tests::migrates_passwords_with_the_key_of_the_browser_that_starts`\n\n### 4. Python `measure_parity` treated Chrome for Testing's default switches as unrequested\n\n`_requested_args_for` counted the restriction switches only when the caller passed `restrictions`. Test: `test_parity_counts_the_default_restrictions_as_requested`.\n\n### Docs and CI\n\n- New [`docs/chrome-for-testing.md`](docs/chrome-for-testing.md), linked from the four READMEs. It covers which download each engine starts, the matching ChromeDriver, the Ubuntu 23.10+ AppArmor sandbox (the library does not add `--no-sandbox` on its own) and the migration key.\n- `js/tests/e2e/chrome-for-testing.e2e.test.js` checks `chrome://version` for each JS engine.
